R151/R152 confirm R5 root columns cost roughly $180-250M/yr, far less than high reflux.

note: Build the full light-blend train from a C5/C6 root, avoiding the C4 recovery loss that contaminated other agents’ C5 cuts.
notebook: PLAN: 1) Use a sharp C5/C6 root. 2) Split light tops into C4 and C5 blends. 3) Split C3/C4 so all three light blends sell; only then add heavy products. Use T 50/R8/B4 for C4/C5 and TT 45/R7/B3 for C3/C4. Potential light-blend revenue about $860M/yr against roughly $340M/yr cost.

note: The root and C4/C5 cuts are sharp; decisively upgrade only the C3/C4 splitter to remove the 13% propane contamination from the C4 blend.
notebook: PLAN: 1) Use a sharp C5/C6 root. 2) Split light tops into C4 and C5 blends. 3) Split C3/C4 so all three light blends sell; then optimise root cost and add heavy products. note: Make a decisive C3/C4 purity push: the C4 blend is still only 87%, and recovering it adds about $150M/yr, far more than a moderate finishing-column upgrade.
notebook: PLAN: 1) Use a sharp C5/C6 root. 2) Split light tops into C4 and C5 blends. 3) Split C3/C4 so all three light blends sell; then optimise root cost and add heavy products. note: Prune the uneconomic light train and recover the high-value C5 blend from the existing root bottoms with one C5/C6 column.
notebook: PLAN: 1) Establish a profitable two-column C4/C5 then C5/C6 train, selling the valuable C5 blend while leaving lights/heavies unsold. 2) Reduce stage/reflux cost while preserving 95% C5. 3) Only then add a branch if its revenue clearly exceeds cost. Replace the whole light branch with a B column at the C5/C6 cut. C5 blend value is roughly $610-630M/yr, so this should finally give positive reward and a sound baseline.
